svg.title: One typed-decision source row at every stage boundary
svg.desc: A vertical worked trace for the first captured source state. It shows the C sharp caller contract, rendered questions, Microsoft tokenizer and Laya preparation, real captured dimensions and selected ID and marker examples, flat ML.NET VBuffer columns versus shaped ONNX Runtime tensors, separate real output shapes, an explicitly illustrative temperature-one softmax calculation, and the real decoded response and typed ML.NET columns.
svg.text: One source row, shown at every boundary
Real preparation and inference facts are separated from one illustrative numeric trace.
REAL / source-backed boundary
ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY / decoder mechanics
1. Caller: options and one State value
OnnxTypedDecisionsOptions { Questions = [priority, quality, actionable],
StateColumnName = "State", BatchSize = 16 }
State = "The customer supplied reproducible steps and requested an urgent fix."
2. Render the fixed questions and assemble the Laya layout
priority / Choice
low | high
quality / Score
level 0: weak | level 1: moderate | level 2: strong
actionable / Noul
false: no, the statement does not hold
true: yes, the statement holds
head chunk: BPE("choice question: How urgent is the request?")
options: [MASK-ID] + BPE(" low"); [MASK-ID] + BPE(" high")
final = [CLS] head [SEP] options [SEP] state [SEP]; marker_pos -> MASK-ID
3. Microsoft.ML.Tokenizers BPE prepares three logical question rows
The tokenizer-only rerun used the pinned vocabulary, merges, config, and profile; no graph or weights.
REAL selected ID slice from priority row
The public stage emits IDs and offsets, not decoded BPE token strings.
Captured preparation boundary: B=3, L=45, K=3; 135 ID positions.
marker_pos priority [11,13] | quality [11,16,21]
actionable [14,24] | mask [T,T,F] [T,T,T] [T,T,F] | qtype [0,1,2]
4. Flat ML.NET vectors become shaped ORT tensors
VBuffer values are flat; scalar dimension columns tell the scorer how to reshape them.
ML.NET: DecisionInputIds VBuffer<long>[135]
DecisionAttentionMask VBuffer<long>[135]
DecisionMarkerPositions VBuffer<long>[9] | DecisionMarkerMask VBuffer<bool>[9]
DecisionQuestionTypes VBuffer<long>[3]
DecisionBatchSize=3; DecisionSequenceLength=45; DecisionMarkerWidth=3
ORT: input_ids Int64[3,45] | attention_mask Int64[3,45]
marker_pos Int64[3,3] | marker_mask Bool[3,3]
qtype Int64[3] | attention=token positions | marker=option slots

g.text: 5. The graph returns logits and a separate action head
REAL retained per-source output after regrouping
logits float[3,3] = 9 slots | act_probs float[3,2] = 6 values
Scored alone: input [3,45]; a combined cursor call may repad [6,46].
act_probs [0.25,0.75] -> select 0.75 directly; no second softmax
The padded slot has numeric storage, but marker_mask excludes it from decoding.
6. Decode the real capture and expose typed results
These values are the accepted first-source-row inference capture, not the illustrative fixture.
Direct Infer returns objects; facade/stages expose typed columns and optional DecisionResults JSON.
Mapped rows borrow fitted resources; the caller owns the fitted transformer.

svg.text: One existing MLNet.TextInference.Onnx package; preparation rerun plus retained inference capture.
No training or native Save/Load claim.
